candidates.visible_reason: Large gray-white wooden member in the upper left with a heavily weathered surface. Pixels show deep lengthwise grain cracks, raised splintered fibers and a frayed, broken end near the center-left.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium. The surface damage is clear, but the frame shows no rail, plate or fastener, so it is unclear whether this is a tie or loose timber debris.
alternatives: loose wood debris or branches rather than an in-track tie
normal weathering or sun-bleaching of old wood
fragment of a previously removed tie left in the ballast

candidates.visible_reason: Cluster of thin, splintered wood strips and slivers in the center, with fibers separated into stringy layers and pieces lying at different angles. A narrow shard sticks up diagonally near the middle.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium to high. The pieces are fragmented and overlapping, so it is hard to tell whether they belong to one in-place member or are scattered remnants.
alternatives: loose broken wood fragments resting on the ballast
leaf litter and debris overlapping the wood
shadow between the strips making the splits look deeper

candidates.visible_reason: Long, weathered wooden piece running diagonally toward the lower right, with a gray, checked and cracked surface. A separate flat plank-like piece lies across the bottom, showing layered, flaking grain along its edge.
candidates.uncertainty: Medium. The wood looks aged and cracked, but the frame is a close-up with no clear tie outline or fastening hardware, so its role is unclear.
alternatives: ordinary surface weathering without structural meaning
ballast stones and plant growth partly covering the wood
